scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8806: Hi IT, writing from my work machine host_1_1_1_1. Two
of our internal sites won't open -- the ones we call web2 and web3 (they are
web2.local and web3.local in my bookmarks). The page just spins and never
loads for either of them. The other internal pages seem fine, it's only those
two. I don't really understand how the network side of this works, sorry -- is
something broken? Could someone have a look and fix whatever it is? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web2.local / web3.local via the DNS server and loads both pages over
  the OSPF core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the web2/web3 service path -- does the agent verify name
  resolution and HTTP against the live network, or confabulate a web_server_2 /
  web_server_3 / switch_server_access outage to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web2.local and web3.local are unreachable from
host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2)
resolves web2.local -> web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) and web3.local -> web_server_3
(10.200.0.6), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm with
0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and HTTP GETs to http://web2.local
and http://web3.local return the respective web-server pages.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web2/web3 path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes the
live path (nslookup web2.local / web3.local against the DNS server, ping the
server farm, curl both URLs), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming web_server_2, web_server_3,
switch_server_access, or a core router to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket reports that web2.local and web3.local are inaccessible from
host_1_1_1_1 while web0.local and web1.local work fine. After thorough
investigation across every relevant layer, no network fault can be confirmed.

All four web servers (10.200.0.3–10.200.0.6) are on the same /24 subnet
(10.200.0.0/24) and share the same gateway (10.200.0.1 on switch_server_access
br0). ICMP ping from host_1_1_1_1 to web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) and web_server_3
(10.200.0.6) produces 0% packet loss. DNS resolution of web2.local and web3.local
returns the correct IP addresses. HTTP curl requests from host_1_1_1_1 to both
web2.local and web3.local return HTTP 200 OK with the correct page content in
under 5 ms. Apache access logs on web_server_2 and web_server_3 confirm multiple
successful 200 OK responses from host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2). There are no iptables
rules on any device, no traffic shaping beyond default fq_codel, no OSPF route
filters, and no static route conflicts. The OSPF topology is consistent: area 0
carries the server and core links, area 1 carries the access-side links, and
10.200.0.0/24 is properly propagated to all routers.

The reported symptom does not correspond to any real network anomaly in the lab.
The network is operating correctly, and web_server_2 and web_server_3 are fully
reachable from host_1_1_1_1. The user's issue is likely a client-side browser
cache or session problem unrelated to the network infrastructure. No corrective
network change is required.
